items.title: Component amplitudes, coherent and incoherent bin laws, and recorded detector weights
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice
hypothesis of the cited Hilbert-space and measure suppliers. Let
$(D,\mathcal A,dx)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space ([[def-measure]]), let
$r\ge1$ be an integer, and let
$$L^{2}(D;\mathbb C^{r}):=\Bigl\{f:D\to\mathbb C^{r}\ \text{measurable}:\ \int_{D}\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx<\infty\Bigr\}\Big/\!\sim,$$
the quotient by equality $dx$-almost everywhere
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]), with
$$\langle f,g\rangle:=\int_{D}\langle f(x),g(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}\,dx,\qquad \|f\|^{2}:=\langle f,f\rangle=\int_{D}\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx,$$
linear in the first argument ([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]).
For $a,b\in L^{2}(D;\mathbb C^{r})$ and measurable $B\subseteq D$ write
$$\langle a,b\rangle_{B}:=\int_{B}\langle a(x),b(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}\,dx,\qquad N:=\|a\|^{2}+\|b\|^{2},\qquad c:=\operatorname{Re}\langle a,b\rangle_{D}.$$
Then:

(a) *Pointwise and integrated cross term.* For $dx$-almost every $x\in D$,
$$\|a(x)+b(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}=\|a(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}+\|b(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}+2\operatorname{Re}\langle a(x),b(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}},$$
and for every measurable $B\subseteq D$, the three functions $\|a\|^{2}$,
$\|b\|^{2}$, $\langle a,b\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}$ being $dx$-integrable on $B$,
$$\int_{B}\|a+b\|^{2}\,dx=\int_{B}\|a\|^{2}\,dx+\int_{B}\|b\|^{2}\,dx+2\operatorname{Re}\langle a,b\rangle_{B}.$$

(b) *Coherent bin law.* If $\|a+b\|>0$, then
$$p_{\mathrm{coh}}(B):=\frac{\displaystyle\int_{B}\|a+b\|^{2}\,dx}{\|a+b\|^{2}}\qquad(B\in\mathcal A)$$
defines a probability measure on $(D,\mathcal A)$
([[def-probability-measure]]), and for every $B\in\mathcal A$ the expansion of
(a) holds with $\|a+b\|^{2}=N+2c$ in the denominator.

(c) *Incoherent bin law.* If $\|a\|>0$, $\|b\|>0$ and $w\in[0,1]$, then
$$p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B):=w\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_{B}\|a\|^{2}\,dx}{\|a\|^{2}}+(1-w)\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_{B}\|b\|^{2}\,dx}{\|b\|^{2}}\qquad(B\in\mathcal A)$$
defines a probability measure on $(D,\mathcal A)$.

(d) *Recorded weights, sub-probability and conditioning.* Let $\mu$ be a
probability measure on $(D,\mathcal A)$ and let $W:D\to[0,1]$ be measurable.
Then $B\mapsto\nu(B):=\int_{B}W\,d\mu$ is a finite measure on $(D,\mathcal A)$
with $0\le\nu(D)\le1$; if $\nu(D)>0$, then
$\bar\nu(B):=\nu(B)/\nu(D)$ defines a probability measure on $(D,\mathcal A)$.
More generally, for finitely many measurable weights $W_{1},\dots,W_{m}:D\to[0,1]$
with $\sum_{a=1}^{m}W_{a}\le1$ pointwise, the numbers
$\nu_{a}:=\int_{D}W_{a}\,d\mu$ satisfy $\nu_{a}\ge0$ and
$\sum_{a=1}^{m}\nu_{a}\le1$; if $\sum_{a=1}^{m}W_{a}=1$ pointwise, then
$\sum_{a=1}^{m}\nu_{a}=1$.

(e) *Coincidence criterion.* Let $\|a\|>0$, $\|b\|>0$ and $\|a+b\|>0$, and put
$w_{*}:=\|a\|^{2}/N$, so that $p_{\mathrm{mix}}$ with weight $w_{*}$ is
$p_{*}(B)=N^{-1}\int_{B}\bigl(\|a\|^{2}+\|b\|^{2}\bigr)dx$. Then
$p_{\mathrm{coh}}(B)=p_{*}(B)$ for every $B\in\mathcal A$ if and only if
$$N\operatorname{Re}\langle a(x),b(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=c\,\bigl(\|a(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}+\|b(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\bigr)\qquad\text{for }dx\text{-almost every }x\in D .$$
In particular, if $\langle a(x),b(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=0$ for almost every
$x$, then the two laws coincide; and if $c=0$, then they coincide if and only
if $\operatorname{Re}\langle a(x),b(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=0$ for almost
every $x$.

The assertions concern the specified classes and weights only; no probability
law of an apparatus, no sample of trials and no empirical claim is asserted.

items.title: The declared two-path preparation model and its ideal detection bins
items.statement:
**(a) Framework data and state convention.** Adopt the state and composition
postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the kinematics and
one-particle model postulate P5, the identical-particle and spin postulate P6,
and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Fix a spin label
$s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$, put $r:=2s+1$, and fix a mass parameter
$m>0$. P5 assigns the one-particle state space
$$H_s:=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^r)$$
with almost-everywhere equivalence classes and pairing
$$\langle f,g\rangle:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\sum_{l=1}^r f_l(x)\overline{g_l(x)}\,dx,$$
linear in the first argument ([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). P1 identifies a pure
preparation with the ray $[\psi]:=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a
unit vector $\psi$ and a general preparation with a density operator, meaning a
bounded self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with
$\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[def-trace-class-operator]],
[[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). Write
$$D(H_s):=\{\rho:\rho\text{ is a bounded self-adjoint positive trace-class operator on }H_s\text{ and }\operatorname{tr}\rho=1\}$$
for the set of general preparations.

For a unit vector $u$, define $P_uf:=\langle f,u\rangle u$. By Cauchy--Schwarz
([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]),
$\|P_uf\|=|\langle f,u\rangle|\le\|f\|$, so $P_u$ is bounded. Then
$P_u^2=P_u$ and $P_u$ is self-adjoint because for $f,g\in H_s$,
$\langle P_uf,g\rangle=\langle f,u\rangle\langle u,g\rangle
=\langle f,P_ug\rangle$. Moreover
$\langle P_uf,f\rangle=|\langle f,u\rangle|^2\ge0$ by the inner-product
identities and $\langle u,u\rangle=1$. Its range is $\mathbb C u$, so it has
finite rank and is trace class by [[def-trace-class-operator]]. The one-term
nuclear representation $P_uf=\langle f,u\rangle u$ gives
$\operatorname{tr}P_u=\langle u,u\rangle=1$ by
[[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]. Thus $P_u$ is a
density operator. For $\psi\ne0$ define
$$\widehat\rho(\psi):=P_{\psi/\|\psi\|},\qquad \widehat\rho(\psi)f=\frac{\langle f,\psi\rangle\psi}{\|\psi\|^2}.$$
For every nonzero scalar $z$, conjugate-linearity in the second argument and
$\|z\psi\|^2=|z|^2\|\psi\|^2$ give
$$\widehat\rho(z\psi)f=\frac{\langle f,z\psi\rangle z\psi}{\|z\psi\|^2}=\frac{|z|^2\langle f,\psi\rangle\psi}{|z|^2\|\psi\|^2}=\widehat\rho(\psi)f,$$
so the pure density operator depends only on the ray.

**Position PVM and Born-density calculation.** P5 assigns the componentwise
position operators $Q_jf=x_jf$ on
$$D(Q_j):=\{f\in H_s:x_jf\in H_s\},\qquad j=1,2,3.$$
Each $Q_j$ is self-adjoint on this domain. To see density, for $f\in H_s$ put
$f_n=\mathbf 1_{\{|x_j|\le n\}}f$; then $f_n\in D(Q_j)$ and $f_n\to f$ in
$H_s$ by dominated convergence. If $f,g\in D(Q_j)$, then
$\langle Q_jf,g\rangle=\langle f,Q_jg\rangle$ because $x_j$ is real-valued
and both products are integrable by Cauchy--Schwarz. If $g\in D(Q_j^*)$ with
$Q_j^*g=h$, let $E_n=\{x:|x_j|\le n\}$. For every $q\in H_s$ supported in
$E_n$, one has $q\in D(Q_j)$ and
$\langle q,(x_jg-h)\mathbf 1_{E_n}\rangle=0$ by the defining adjoint
identity. The vector $(x_jg-h)\mathbf 1_{E_n}$ lies in $H_s$ because $x_j$
is bounded on $E_n$; taking it for $q$ shows $x_jg=h$ almost everywhere on
$E_n$. Since $E_n\uparrow\mathbb R^3$, $x_jg=h\in H_s$ almost everywhere,
so $g\in D(Q_j)$ and $Q_j^*g=Q_jg$. Symmetry gives the reverse domain
inclusion; hence $Q_j=Q_j^*$ by
[[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]].

For a Borel set $S\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, define the indicator multiplication
operator $M_{\mathbf 1_S}:H_s\to H_s$ by
$(M_{\mathbf 1_S}f)(x):=\mathbf 1_S(x)f(x)$ almost everywhere. This is
independent of the representative of the $L^2$ class and is bounded, since
$$\|M_{\mathbf 1_S}f\|^2=\int_S\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^r}^2dx\le\|f\|^2.$$
It is linear and a bounded operator with bound one
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). It is an orthogonal projection:
$\mathbf 1_S^2=\mathbf 1_S$ and the real indicator multiplier is
self-adjoint for the declared pairing.

For Borel $C\subseteq\mathbb R$, define
$$E_j(C):=M_{\mathbf 1_{\{x:x_j\in C\}}}.$$
Each value is a bounded orthogonal projection since
$\|\mathbf 1_{\{x:x_j\in C\}}f\|\le\|f\|$, and
$E_j(\varnothing)=0$,
$E_j(\mathbb R)=I$, and $E_j(C\cap D)=E_j(C)E_j(D)$. For a disjoint sequence
$(C_n)$ with union $C$, the squared norm of
$E_j(C)f-\sum_{n\le N}E_j(C_n)f$ equals
$$\int_{\{x:x_j\in C\setminus\cup_{n\le N}C_n\}}\|f(x)\|^2dx,$$
which tends to zero by dominated convergence; hence $E_j$ is strongly
countably additive. Its scalar measures are finite Borel measures
$$\langle E_j(C)f,f\rangle=\int_{\{x:x_j\in C\}}\|f(x)\|^2dx,$$
and are regular on $\mathbb R$ by
[[cor-second-countable-lch-locally-finite-borel-measures-are-regular]]. The
push-forward integral identity
$$\int_{\mathbb R}g(\lambda)d\langle E_j(\lambda)f,f\rangle =\int_{\mathbb R^3}g(x_j)\|f(x)\|^2dx$$
holds first for indicators and nonnegative simple functions and then for
nonnegative measurable $g$ by monotone convergence. In particular the domain
of $\int\lambda\,dE_j(\lambda)$ is exactly $D(Q_j)$ by the same identity
with $g(\lambda)=\lambda^2$. For bounded Borel $g$, the bounded PVM calculus
equals multiplication by $g(x_j)$: this holds for indicators by the
definition of $E_j$, for finite simple functions by linearity, and for bounded
Borel functions by uniform simple approximation and the norm bound of the
bounded calculus ([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]). Therefore the
truncations of the unbounded integral are multiplication by
$x_j\mathbf 1_{\{|x_j|\le n\}}$. For $f\in D(Q_j)$ these converge in $H_s$
to $x_jf$, since the squared tail norm is
$\int_{\{|x_j|>n\}}x_j^2\|f(x)\|^2dx\to0$ by dominated convergence. Thus
$\int\lambda\,dE_j(\lambda)=Q_j$ on exactly $D(Q_j)$, and the regular spectral
theorem identifies $E_j$ as the spectral PVM of $Q_j$
([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]],
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]).

Define the joint position PVM by
$$G(B):=M_{\mathbf 1_B}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R^3\text{ Borel}).$$
For each $f$, $\|G(B)f\|\le\|f\|$, so its values are bounded; indicator
multiplication gives its projection, identity, and intersection laws. Strong
countable additivity follows from dominated convergence applied to $\|f\|^2$.
Its scalar measures are $B\mapsto\int_B\|f(x)\|^2dx$, finite
regular Borel measures on $\mathbb R^3$. On coordinate rectangles,
$$G(C_1\times C_2\times C_3)=E_1(C_1)E_2(C_2)E_3(C_3).$$
The rectangles generate $\mathcal B(\mathbb R^3)$; the published Borel-product
and finite-measure uniqueness theorems show that these rectangle values
uniquely determine the joint PVM ([[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]],
[[lem-finite-measure-uniqueness-on-a-pi-system]],
[[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]): for any two candidate PVMs,
their finite scalar measures agree on the generating rectangles and on the
whole space, so they agree on every Borel set; the polarization identity in
the last lemma then gives equality of the operator values. This constructs the
mathematical joint position PVM; a physical joint detector reading is supplied
only for the finite effect families declared below. For a density operator
$\rho$ define
$\mu^G_\rho(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho G(B))$ for each Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$. Since $G$ is a PVM, this set function is a probability
measure by the general density/PVM calculation used in clause (ii) of P2. For a
finite Borel partition $(B_a)_{a=1}^m$,
the operators $G(B_a)$ are orthogonal projections and sum to $I$. For each
$f\in H_s$,
$\langle G(B_a)f,f\rangle=\|G(B_a)f\|^2\in[0,\|f\|^2]$, so they are
bounded effects with $0\le G(B_a)\le I$ in quadratic-form order. Clause (iv)
of P2 therefore assigns the channel probabilities
$p_a(\rho)=\mu^G_\rho(B_a)$; the two-channel partition
$(B,\mathbb R^3\setminus B)$ assigns $\mu^G_\rho(B)$ to bin $B$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]). Thus $G$ is the
mathematical joint position PVM, while the detector reading used here is the
declared finite-effect model of P2(iv); this does not assert that every three
sharp coordinate measurement is jointly realized by a laboratory apparatus.
For a unit vector $u$, the trace formula for the rank-one operator $P_u$ gives
$$\mu^G_{P_u}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(P_uG(B))=\|G(B)u\|^2=\int_B\|u(x)\|_{\mathbb C^r}^2dx,$$
and P7(iii) leaves identification of this ideal detector with a concrete
apparatus as a tested physical claim with uncertainty.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as required by
the cited trace and spectral suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Declared two-path assignment.** A **declared two-path preparation model**
of the apparatus is the assignment of two nonzero classes
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\in H_{s}$, called the **path components** of the model with
respect to the declared pair of alternative path conditions of the apparatus,
together with a declared **relative phase** $\varphi\in\mathbb R$ and a declared
**weight** $w\in[0,1]$. The assignment of $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}$, $\varphi$ and
$w$ is part of the preparation model in the sense of clause (i) of P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]): it is declared, not
computed from the framework, and no item of this page asserts that a particle
described by the model "took" one of the two paths.

**(c) Coherent preparation.** The declared two-path model is **admissible at
phase $\varphi$** when $\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\ne0$ in $H_{s}$. When it
is admissible, the **coherent preparation** of relative phase $\varphi$ is the
pure preparation
$$\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi):=\widehat\rho\bigl(\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\bigr),$$
the normalized rank-one density operator defined in clause (a). The relative
phase $\varphi$ is read in radians (dimensionless). Multiplying both path
components by one common nonzero scalar leaves their associated pure density
operator unchanged, while the declared relative phase remains part of the
preparation assignment.

**(d) Incoherent preparation.** For a declared weight $w\in[0,1]$ the
**incoherent preparation**, or **which-path preparation**, of the model is
$$\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w):=w\,\widehat\rho(\psi_{1})+(1-w)\,\widehat\rho(\psi_{2}).$$
It is a density operator: both summands are positive trace-class operators of
trace one; trace-class operators form a vector space, nonnegative real
combinations preserve positivity and self-adjointness, and the trace is linear,
so $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w)=w+(1-w)=1$
([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]],
[[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). The weight $w$
is a declared preparation weight, not an outcome probability.

**(e) Ideal detection bins.** A **declared ideal detector** of the model is a
finite family $\mathcal B=(B_{a})_{a=1}^{m}$ of pairwise disjoint Borel subsets
of $\mathbb R^{3}$ with $\bigcup_{a}B_{a}=\mathbb R^{3}$; the **ideal bin
probabilities** of a preparation $\rho\in D(H_{s})$ are the numbers
$$p_{a}(\rho):=\mu^{G}_{\rho}(B_{a})=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,G(B_{a})\bigr)\qquad(a=1,\dots,m),$$
the reading of the finite-effect clause (iv) of P2 for the declared detector
and its mathematical joint position PVM
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]). By clause (iv) of P2 these numbers are
nonnegative, are at most one, and satisfy
$\sum_{a}p_{a}(\rho)=1$. A single **declared bin** $B$ is the two-element ideal
detector $(B,\mathbb R^{3}\setminus B)$; its probability is $\mu^{G}_{\rho}(B)$.

For the **ideal support**, choose a Lebesgue-measurable representative $f$ of
the unit $L^2$ class and form $S_f:=\{x:\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^r}>0\}$. The
ideal support is the class of $S_f$ under equality up to a Lebesgue-null
symmetric difference. This class is independent of the representative, and
it is not asserted to be a Borel detector bin.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the model data of the pair:
the framework reading, the declared path components and preparations, and the
ideal bin reading of the position observable. They adopt no assumption beyond
P1, P2, P5, P6, P7 and the cited mathematics; the declaration of
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2},\varphi,w$ and of the bins is an apparatus-model input, and
the claim that a concrete two-slit apparatus realizes a particular such
declaration is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7(iii). The
declared bins are subsets of $\mathbb R^{3}$; the model does not claim that a
physical screen of lower dimension is literally a spatial region, and a
marginal, coarse-graining or flux reduction of a state to a screen coordinate
or surface is a separate detection model, not supplied here. No dynamics, no
recorded-event response, no sampling model and no empirical result is
asserted; the recorded-event and sampling models are declared separately on
this page.

items.physical_scope: A declared preparation and detection model for a two-path interference arrangement in the massive spin-s model of the framework: two declared nonzero path-component classes of the model state space, the coherent preparations of a declared relative phase, the declared incoherent (which-path) preparations with declared weights, and the ideal detection-bin reading of the model's joint position observable. The model is a declaration of the apparatus and preparation assignment in the sense of the preparation and apparatus postulate P7; it asserts no derivation of the path decomposition from the framework, no claim that any particle took a definite path, no detector response or sampling model, no experiment and no empirical result. Spatial bins are regions of R^3; a lower-dimensional material screen and any marginal or flux reduction of a state to it are separate models, not claimed here.

items.title: The declared recorded detector and sampling model of the two-path arrangement
items.statement:
Adopt the declared two-path preparation model of
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]], the
unsharp finite-outcome clause (iv) of the observable and probability postulate
P2, and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). The following vocabulary is used
by this page.

**(a) Declared recorded detector.** A **declared recorded detector** of the
arrangement is a finite set $A$ of **recorded outcome labels** with
$0\notin A$, together with measurable **recorded weights**
$w_{a}:\mathbb R^{3}\to[0,1]$ for $a\in A$ such that
$\sum_{a\in A}w_{a}(x)\le1$ for almost every $x\in\mathbb R^{3}$. The
**effect** of the label $a$ is the multiplication operator
$$F_{a}:=M_{w_{a}},\qquad (M_{w}\psi)(x):=w(x)\psi(x)\quad\text{a.e.},$$
on $H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, and the **no-record effect** is
$$F_{0}:=I-\sum_{a\in A}F_{a}.$$
The multiplier is a well-defined linear map on almost-everywhere classes,
since changing a representative on a null set changes its product only on
that null set.
Each $F_a$ is bounded: for $\psi\in H_s$,
$$\|M_{w_a}\psi\|^2=\int_{\mathbb R^3}w_a(x)^2\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^r}^2dx\le\|\psi\|^2,$$
so the boundedness inequality holds with bound $C=1$ by monotonicity of the
nonnegative integral ([[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]).
Thus $F_a$ is a bounded linear operator ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Because $w_a$
is real, the componentwise pairing gives
$\langle M_{w_a}\psi,\phi\rangle=\langle\psi,M_{w_a}\phi\rangle$ for all
$\psi,\phi\in H_s$; hence $F_a$ is self-adjoint by
[[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]. At almost every $x$, the finite-dimensional
operator $w_a(x)I_{\mathbb C^r}$ is nonnegative in the sense of
[[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]], and therefore
$$0\le\langle F_a\psi,\psi\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R^3}w_a(x)\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^r}^2dx\le\|\psi\|^2.$$
Here $0\le F_a\le I$ means these quadratic-form inequalities for every
$\psi\in H_s$.

Define $w_0(x):=\max\{0,1-\sum_{a\in A}w_a(x)\}$. This is measurable,
$0\le w_0\le1$, and it equals $1-\sum_aw_a$ almost everywhere by the
admissibility condition. Thus $F_0=M_{w_0}=I-\sum_aF_a$ on $H_s$, and the
same argument gives $0\le F_0\le I$ and self-adjointness. Consequently
$\sum_{a\in A}F_a+F_0=I$, so the completed family is a finite family of
bounded effects of clause (iv) of P2
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]).

**(b) Recorded probabilities.** For a preparation $\rho\in D(H_{s})$ the
**recorded probability** of a label $a\in A$ and the **no-record probability**
are
$$\nu(a):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho F_{a}\bigr),\qquad \nu(0):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho F_{0}\bigr)=1-\sum_{a\in A}\nu(a),$$
the outcome reading of clause (iv) of P2 for the declared effects
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (f)
records the reading; the numbers are nonnegative and sum to one). The
**recorded-event mass** is $\nu(A):=\sum_{a\in A}\nu(a)=1-\nu(0)\in[0,1]$. A
detector is **full-efficiency** when $\sum_{a}w_{a}=1$ almost everywhere, so
that $F_{0}=0$ and $\nu(0)=0$ for every preparation. For a fixed preparation
$\rho$, the model **loses** events when $\nu(0)>0$, and the no-record channel
carries this lost mass. A detector that is not full-efficiency can nevertheless
have $\nu(0)=0$ for a particular preparation. A **declared recorded bin** $B$ is
the special case with one label $a$ and $w_{a}=\mathbf 1_{B}$; then
$F_{a}=G(B)$ is the position projection of clause (e) of
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]], with the
position set $B$ read in the metre unit of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and the recorded probability is
the ideal bin probability.

**(c) Loss conditioning.** When $\nu(A)>0$, the **conditioned recorded law** is
$$\bar\nu(a):=\frac{\nu(a)}{\nu(A)}\qquad(a\in A).$$
It is a probability measure on the finite set $A$
([[def-probability-measure]]); it is the law of the recorded label under the
declared model conditioned on the occurrence of a record. Conditioning is a
statistical operation on the recorded data; it is not a state update, and no
claim of P3 is made here.

**(d) Sampling model.** A **declared $N$-trial sampling model** for a fixed
preparation $\rho$ is a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$
carrying measurable maps
$O_{1},\dots,O_{N}:(\Omega,\mathcal F)\to
(A\cup\{0\},\mathcal P(A\cup\{0\}))$ ($N\ge1$), where $0$ is the no-record
label of clause (b) and is distinct from every recorded label because
$0\notin A$. The maps are **mutually independent** in the sense of
[[def-independence-of-finite-random-variables]] and **identically distributed**
with $\mathbb P(O_{k}=a)=\nu(a)$ for every $a\in A$, $\mathbb P(O_{k}=0)=\nu(0)$
and every $k$, where $\nu$ is the recorded law of clause (b); the numbers
$\nu(a)$ and $\nu(0)$ sum to one, so this is a probability law on the finite
set $A\cup\{0\}$. The **empirical frequency** of the label $a$ in the sample is
$$F_{N}(a):=\frac{1}{N}\#\{k:O_{k}=a\}.$$
A **declared fringe criterion** for sample size $N$ is a subset
$C\subseteq(A\cup\{0\})^{N}$; the model **accepts** the sample when
$(O_{1},\dots,O_{N})\in C$ and **fails the criterion** otherwise. The
identification of repetitions of a concrete procedure with the independent
identically distributed model is an additional statistical assumption in the
sense of clause (ii) of P7; it is not a consequence of P1-P6, and correlated
trials, drifting preparation, dead time and selection must be modeled or
recorded as limitations if present ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

**(e) Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) fix the recorded-detector and sampling
vocabulary of the pair and read clause (iv) of P2 and clauses (i)-(iii) of P7.
The recorded weights, the label set, the conditioning convention and the
sampling model are declared apparatus and procedure inputs. The claim "this
apparatus realizes the effect family $F_{a}$" and the claim "its repetitions
are independent and identically distributed draws of $\nu$" are physical
identifications with uncertainty under P7(iii) and P7(ii), can fail, and are
not derived here. No calibration, efficiency, background or resolution value
is asserted, no counts are recorded, and no statistical-inference conclusion
is drawn by this definition.

items.title: Coherent and which-path detection laws of the declared two-path model
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the
internal-factor postulate P6, as read by
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]], and the
preparation and apparatus discipline P7, and adopt the declared two-path
preparation model of that definition with path components
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\in H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, relative phase
$\varphi\in\mathbb R$ and weight $w\in[0,1]$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}}$ be the joint position
PVM constructed in clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]], and read
its outcome law by P2 as $\mu^{G}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho G(B))$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]). Put
$$N:=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2},\qquad Z(B):=\int_{B}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}dx,\qquad Z:=Z(\mathbb R^{3}),\qquad c(B):=\operatorname{Re}Z(B),\qquad c:=c(\mathbb R^{3}).$$
Then:

(a) *Coherent law.* If the declared model is admissible at phase $\varphi$,
then for every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$
$$\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi)}(B)=\frac{\displaystyle\int_{B}\|\psi_{1}(x)+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx}{\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\|^{2}} ,$$
and the numerator expands as
$$\int_{B}\bigl(\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}\bigr)dx+2\operatorname{Re}\Bigl(e^{-i\varphi}\int_{B}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}dx\Bigr),$$
with denominator $N+2\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\varphi}Z)$; in particular
$\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\|^{2}>0$.

(b) *Which-path law.* For the declared weight $w\in[0,1]$ and every Borel set
$B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$,
$$\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w)}(B)=w\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_{B}\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}\,dx}{\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}}+(1-w)\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_{B}\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}\,dx}{\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}} .$$

(c) *Coincidence criterion.* Let $w_{*}:=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}/N$, so that
$\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w_{*})}(B)=N^{-1}\int_{B}(\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2})dx$.
If the declared model is admissible at phase $0$, then
$\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(0)}(B)=\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w_{*})}(B)$
for every Borel set $B$ if and only if
$$N\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=c\,\bigl(\|\psi_{1}(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}+\|\psi_{2}(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\bigr)\qquad\text{for almost every }x .$$
In particular, if $\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=0$ for
almost every $x$, then the coherent law of phase $0$ and the which-path law of
weight $w_{*}$ agree on every bin; and if $c=0$, then, under phase-$0$
admissibility, they agree if and only if
$\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=0$ for
almost every $x$.

(d) *Scope.* Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional on P1, P2, P5, P6 and the
declared model, and identify the laws of exactly two declared preparations.
They assert no path ontology, use no entangled marker state and no reduced
state, assert no detector response, no loss, no sampling model, no dynamics and
no empirical result.

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 1.2 printed pages 5-6 and Section 1.4 printed page 15 (PDF page 23): amplitudes for alternative routes, the interference cross term, and coherent versus incoherent preparation

items.physical_scope: The detection laws of the declared two-path preparation model of the massive spin-s model of the framework: the normalized coherent bin law with its amplitude cross term, the which-path (incoherent) bin law, and the criterion under which the two declared laws coincide on every bin, with the phase-zero criterion conditional on the coherent preparation being admissible at phase zero. The statement is a conditional consequence of P1, P2, P5 and P6, the declared apparatus and preparation assignment in the sense of P7, and the cited published mathematics plus the local calculations in its proof. items.title: Recorded bin laws, loss and conditioning of the declared two-path detector
items.statement:
Adopt the observable and probability postulate P2 in its unsharp finite-outcome
reading, the declared two-path preparation model
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]] with path
components $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\ne0$, relative phase $\varphi$ and weight $w$, and
the declared recorded detector
[[def-nrqm-interference-recorded-detector-and-sampling-model]] with finite
label set $A$ satisfying $0\notin A$, recorded weights $w_{a}$ and effects
$F_{a}=M_{w_{a}}$, no-record
effect $F_{0}=I-\sum_{a}F_{a}$, recorded probabilities $\nu(a)$ and recorded-event
mass $\nu(A)=\sum_{a\in A}\nu(a)$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited trace-class,
rank-one and square-root suppliers. Let
$\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi)$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w)$ be the declared
coherent and which-path preparations and put $N:=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}$,
$c:=\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle$ and
$w_{*}:=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}/N$. Then:

(a) *Recorded coherent law.* If the model is admissible at phase $\varphi$,
then for every label $a\in A$
$$\nu_{\mathrm{coh}(\varphi)}(a)=\frac{\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}w_{a}(x)\,\|\psi_{1}(x)+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx}{\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi}\psi_{2}\|^{2}} ,$$
and the numerator equals
$$\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}w_{a}\bigl(\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}\bigr)dx+2\operatorname{Re}\Bigl(e^{-i\varphi}\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}w_{a}\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}dx\Bigr).$$

(b) *Recorded which-path law.* For the declared weight $w\in[0,1]$ and every
$a\in A$,
$$\nu_{\mathrm{mix}(w)}(a)=w\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}w_{a}\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}dx}{\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}}+(1-w)\,\frac{\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}w_{a}\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}dx}{\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}} .$$

(c) *Loss.* The no-record probability is
$\nu(0)=1-\nu(A)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{0})\ge0$, so $\nu(A)\le1$. If
$\sum_{a}w_{a}=1$ almost everywhere, then $F_{0}=0$ and $\nu(0)=0$ for every
preparation; if $F_{0}\ne0$, then there is a declared pure preparation with
$\nu(0)>0$. When $\nu(A)>0$, the conditioned recorded law
$\bar\nu(a)=\nu(a)/\nu(A)$ is a probability measure on $A$.

(d) *Ideal bins and coincidence.* If $w_{a}=\mathbf 1_{B_{a}}$ for a declared
ideal detector $(B_{a})_{a=1}^{m}$, then
$\nu(a)=\mu^{G}_{\rho}(B_{a})$ is the ideal bin probability of
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]]. Moreover, if
the declared model is admissible at phase $0$ and if
the almost-everywhere relation
$$N\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}=c\,\bigl(\|\psi_{1}(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}+\|\psi_{2}(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\bigr)$$
of clause (c) of that theorem holds, then the recorded coherent law of phase
$0$ and the recorded which-path law of weight $w_{*}$ agree, $\nu_{\mathrm{coh}(0)}(a)=\nu_{\mathrm{mix}(w_{*})}(a)$,
for every label $a$ of every declared recorded detector.

(e) *Scope.* Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional on P2, the declared preparation
and detector models and the cited mathematics; they assert no calibration, no
resolution, background or efficiency value, no state update, no counts and no
empirical result, and the claim that a concrete apparatus realizes the declared
effects is a tested identification with uncertainty.

D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Sections 1.1-1.2, printed pages 3-14 (PDF pages 6-17): detection records and the probability law of the wave function

items.title: Continuity equation and local balance for the massive-model position density
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 with its internal-factor postulate P6,
read through [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] and
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]). Assume Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $V_0\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ be the
real bounded measurable P5 potential and choose a bounded real measurable
representative $V:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$; on $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$
use its restriction. Fix the P5 constants $\hbar>0$ and $m>0$, a spin label
$s$ with $r=2s+1$, a nonempty
open spatial region $\Omega$, and a nonempty open time interval
$I\subseteq\mathbb R$. Let $\psi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb C^r$ have
components $\psi_l$, $\partial_t\psi_l$, $\partial_j\psi_l$ and
$\partial_k\partial_j\psi_l$ continuous on $\Omega\times I$ for all
$j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$, and suppose the **model equation** holds for Lebesgue
almost every $(x,t)\in\Omega\times I$:
$$i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi_l(x,t)=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta\psi_l(x,t)+V(x)\psi_l(x,t)\qquad(l=1,\dots,r).$$
The displayed equation is the local differential expression assigned by
P5/P4; it is a hypothesis here, and $\psi$ is not required to be a global P4
domain vector. P5 assigns $H_{\mathrm{op}}=-\hbar^2\Delta/(2m)+V(Q)$ on the
componentwise $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^r)$ domain, and P4 asserts the
norm-differentiable equation for vectors in that domain. Existence of a smooth
representative for such a global solution is a separate regularity hypothesis
([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]
clause (iv), [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] clause (iii)).

Define the **squared-amplitude density** and its associated **current** by
$$n(x,t):=\sum_{l=1}^r|\psi_l(x,t)|^2=\|\psi(x,t)\|_{\mathbb C^r}^2,\qquad j(x,t):=\frac{\hbar}{m}\sum_{l=1}^r\operatorname{Im}(\overline{\psi_l(x,t)}\,\nabla\psi_l(x,t))=-\frac{\hbar}{m}\operatorname{Im}\langle\psi(x,t),\nabla\psi(x,t)\rangle_{\mathbb C^r}.$$
For $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$, when $\psi(\cdot,t)$ is a unit vector of $H_s$,
$n(\cdot,t)$ is the model's position probability density. Under the local
hypotheses stated here, no global normalization or $H_s$ membership is assumed;
$n$ is the squared-amplitude density and the same balance equations apply.
Accordingly, $j$ is the probability current for a normalized state and the
corresponding squared-amplitude current otherwise.
The minus sign in the pairing expression follows from the convention that the
$L^2$ pairing is linear in its first argument. For each component put
$j_l=(\hbar/m)\operatorname{Im}(\overline{\psi_l}\nabla\psi_l)$.
Then:

(a) *Pointwise continuity.* For every $(x,t)\in\Omega\times I$,
$$\partial_{t}n(x,t)+\operatorname{div}j(x,t)=0 .$$

(b) *Integrated balance.* If $D\subseteq\Omega$ is a bounded open set with
$C^{1}$ boundary and $\overline D\subseteq\Omega$
([[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]]), then
$t\mapsto\int_Dn(x,t)dx$ is differentiable on $I$ with
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{D}n(x,t)\,dx=-\int_{\partial D}j(x,t)\cdot\nu(x)\,dS ,$$
$\nu$ the outward unit normal.

(c) *Global conservation under domination.* If $\Omega=\mathbb R^{3}$, if for
each $l$ there is a nonnegative measurable $g_l\in L^{1}(\mathbb R^{3})$ with
$|\psi_{l}(x,t)|^{2}\le g_{l}(x)$ for almost every $x$ and every $t\in I$, and
if
$$\lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_{t\in I}\int_{\{|x|=R\}}|j_l(x,t)|\,dS=0$$
for each $l$, then $t\mapsto\int_{\mathbb R^3}n(x,t)dx$ is finite and
constant on $I$. In particular, if this integral is $1$ at one time, it is
$1$ throughout $I$ and $n(\cdot,t)$ is a position probability density at every
time.

(d) *Flow conservation.* For the model's assigned unitary flow
$U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$ on the model's state space and every
$\psi_{0}\in H_{s}$, one has $\|U(t)\psi_{0}\|=\|\psi_{0}\|$ for every
$t\in\mathbb R$; consequently the model's position probability of a unit
preparation integrates to one at every time, without the regularity hypotheses
of (a)-(c), because P4 assigns a unitary group
([[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (b)).

(e) *Units, reading and scope.* In the SI conventions of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] the position wave function has
unit $\mathrm m^{-3/2}$, the density $n$ has unit
$\mathrm m^{-3}$ and the current $j$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-2}\mathrm s^{-1}$;
the display of (a) is the local balance of the model's squared-amplitude density
in its smooth regime, and (b) reads the rate of change of its integral over a
region as minus the outward current flux across its boundary. When $\psi$ is a
normalized full-space state, these are the position probability density and
probability flux, respectively. The
statement does not assert that the flow of an arbitrary $L^{2}$ initial vector
has a representative obeying the regularity hypotheses of (a)-(c), does not
identify a recorded screen rate or any detection law with the surface flux (the
detection model of this page is the declared effect and bin model), and records
no empirical result.

references.title: D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 1.2, printed pages 9-13 (PDF pages 12-16): the Schroedinger equation and conservation of total probability; Section 1.3 printed pages 14-18: the probability current
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 2.3 printed pages 32-33 (PDF pages 40-41): the probability current, the continuity equation and the surface-flux balance

items.physical_scope: The local squared-amplitude balance of the massive spin-s model in its smooth solution regime: for a componentwise C1-in-time, C2-in-space function satisfying the displayed local Schroedinger equation almost everywhere with the real bounded measurable P5 potential on an open spatial region, its squared-amplitude density and current satisfy the pointwise continuity equation and integrated balance over bounded C1 regions. On an open time interval, its finite total squared-amplitude integral is conserved under explicit domination and surface-flux hypotheses; if normalized at one time, it remains a position probability density. Separately, the P4 unitary flow preserves the norm of every state and the P2 position probability of every unit preparation has total mass one. The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the cited published mathematics. It does not assert that the flow of an arbitrary L2 initial vector has a C1-in-time, C2-in-space representative, identify a screen record rate with surface flux, or record an empirical result.

items.title: A finite sample can fail a criterion that rejects a positive-probability sequence
items.statement:
Adopt the declared two-path preparation model
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]] and the
declared recorded detector and sampling model
[[def-nrqm-interference-recorded-detector-and-sampling-model]] with finite
label set $A$ satisfying $0\notin A$, recorded law $\nu$ (a probability law
on $A\cup\{0\}$, with $0$ the distinct no-record label), and the declared
$N$-trial sampling model of clause (d)
of that definition; the identification of repetitions with that model is the
additional statistical assumption of clause (ii) of the preparation and
apparatus postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).
Fix a preparation $\rho$, which may be a coherent preparation
$\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi)$ or a which-path preparation
$\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w)$ of the declared model, so that its recorded law is the
law $\nu$ of [[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-recorded-bin-laws-loss-and-conditioning]]. Let
$(O_{1},\dots,O_{N})$ be the outcome sequence,
$S_{N}(a):=\#\{k:O_{k}=a\}$ and $F_{N}(a):=S_{N}(a)/N$ the empirical frequency
of $a\in A\cup\{0\}$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]). Then:

(a) *Concentration.* For every label $a$ and every $\varepsilon>0$,
$$\mathbb E\bigl[F_{N}(a)\bigr]=\nu(a),\qquad \operatorname{Var}\bigl(F_{N}(a)\bigr)=\frac{\nu(a)\bigl(1-\nu(a)\bigr)}{N},\qquad \mathbb P\bigl(|F_{N}(a)-\nu(a)|\ge\varepsilon\bigr)\le\frac{\nu(a)(1-\nu(a))}{N\varepsilon^{2}} .$$

(b) *Positive failure probability.* Let $C\subseteq(A\cup\{0\})^{N}$ be a
declared fringe criterion, and suppose there is a sequence
$(a_{1},\dots,a_{N})$ with $(a_{1},\dots,a_{N})\notin C$ and $\nu(a_{k})>0$ for
every $k$. Then the failure probability of the criterion is
$$\mathbb P\bigl((O_{1},\dots,O_{N})\notin C\bigr)\ge\prod_{k=1}^{N}\nu(a_{k})>0 .$$
In particular, if $\nu(a)>0$ for some label $a$, then every criterion that
rejects the constant sequence $(a,\dots,a)$ has failure probability at least
$\nu(a)^{N}>0$.

(c) *No discrimination between coincident laws.* If the model is admissible
at phase $0$ and the recorded coherent law of phase $0$ and the recorded
which-path law of weight $w_{*}$ coincide in the sense of clause (d) of
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-recorded-bin-laws-loss-and-conditioning]], then no
criterion whatsoever has different probability of acceptance under the two
declared preparations; in particular no finite sample distinguishes them with
certainty.

(d) *Scope.* Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional on the declared preparation,
detector and sampling models and the cited mathematics. The independence and
identical distribution of the trials are declared model assumptions, not
consequences of P1-P6; no failure probability, error rate, p-value, confidence
level, power, sample size or measured count is computed or asserted, and no
conclusion is drawn about any real apparatus. In particular the statements do
not assert that a coherent preparation must show a visible fringe pattern in a
finite sample, and do not assert that a sample without a visible pattern
falsifies the coherent model.

references.title: D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 1.3, printed pages 14-18 (PDF pages 17-21): the two-slit interference probability density and the accumulation of detection records
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 1.2 printed pages 5-6: amplitudes, probabilities and the accumulation of repeated measurements

items.physical_scope: A hypothetical finite-sampling analysis of the declared two-path arrangement: for a coherent or which-path preparation whose recorded law is fixed, and under the declared independent-and-identically-distributed $N$-trial sampling model, every declared fringe criterion that rejects at least one outcome sequence of positive probability fails with positive probability, and the empirical frequency of a label concentrates around its recorded probability. The indistinguishability conclusion for the phase-zero coherent and weighted which-path laws assumes that phase zero is admissible. The item is a conditional consequence of the declared preparation and detector models, the declared sampling model in the sense of P7, and published probability suppliers with local calculations. It asserts no measured counts, no p-value, no confidence level, no universal failure probability, and no empirical conclusion about nature; a finite sample without a visible fringe pattern is not a falsification of the coherent model, and a sample with a visible pattern is not a proof of it.

items.title: What the two-path detection page establishes, assumes and defers
items.statement:
## Scope of the page

**What is established.** The page declares the two-path preparation model
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]] with its
path components, coherent and which-path preparations and ideal detection bins,
and the recorded detector and sampling model
[[def-nrqm-interference-recorded-detector-and-sampling-model]] with its bounded
effects, no-record channel, loss conditioning and declared independent trials.
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]] derives the
normalized coherent bin law with its amplitude cross term, the which-path bin
law, and the criterion under which the two declared laws coincide on every bin;
the criterion comparing phase $0$ is conditional on the model being admissible
at phase $0$.
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-recorded-bin-laws-loss-and-conditioning]] derives the
recorded-bin laws, the no-record mass and conditioned law, the reduction of
indicator weights to ideal bins, and a sufficient condition for the recorded
laws to coincide when the model is admissible at phase $0$.
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-continuity-and-local-probability-balance]]
derives the continuity equation and local squared-amplitude balance for
componentwise $C^1$-in-time, $C^2$-in-space solutions of the P4/P5 equation
almost everywhere with the bounded measurable P5 potential. This density is a
position probability density when the full-space state is normalized; under
the theorem's domination and surface-flux hypotheses its finite total
squared-amplitude integral is conserved on an interval. P4 separately gives
norm conservation of the model's flow and total probability one for unit
preparations.
[[texp-nrqm-interference-finite-sample-fringe-failure]] shows that, within the
declared independent-trials model, a declared fringe criterion that rejects a
positive-probability outcome sequence fails with positive probability, and
that no criterion distinguishes two recorded laws that coincide.

**Adopted rather than derived.** The path components, the relative phase, the
preparation weight, the recorded weights and the independence of trials are
declarations of the preparation and apparatus models in the sense of P7; the
identification of a concrete arrangement with these declarations is a tested
identification with uncertainty and can fail. The appearance of an
interference pattern is not derived for any laboratory apparatus, and no
count, efficiency, resolution, background or calibration value appears on this
page.

**Not claimed.** The page does not assert which-path ontology, does not assign
a trajectory to the particle between preparation and detection, and does not
claim that the coherent preparation is the only admissible model of any
apparatus. It makes no claim that a lower-dimensional screen is a spatial
region of the model: a marginal, coarse-graining or flux reduction of a state
to a screen coordinate or surface is a separate detection model. It also makes
none of the following claims: that the flow of an arbitrary $L^{2}$ initial
vector has a $C^{2}$ representative; that a recorded screen rate equals the
surface flux; or that agreement of a finite dataset with a declared law
establishes the framework.

**Deferred content and destinations.** Visibility loss by path marking and
entanglement is not established here: the reusable marker-overlap physical
result is homed on the entanglement page
`qm-composites-entanglement-and-reduced-states`, and this page neither states
nor consumes it. Photon polarization and optical interference are out of scope
and belong to the photon and radiation page; the electron double-slit report is
reported on the companion examples page, not here. Comparative classical field
models and quantum-versus-classical model selection are likewise separate
models.

**Evidence status.** The page contains no experiment and no measured value;
the bounded, conditional statements above are consequences of the cited
postulates, declarations and mathematics. The companion examples page reports
one source-backed electron double-slit experiment with its disclosed
limitations, and that report tests the combined model and apparatus
assumptions rather than proving them.

items.title: An ideal flat two-path distribution: exact coherent and which-path bin laws
items.statement:
Adopt the declared two-path preparation and detection model
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]] in its
spin-zero reading $r=1$, and the coherent and which-path detection laws
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]]. Assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]), as required by the preparation and detection-law
suppliers. Fix lengths
$0<d<L<\infty$, measured in metres, and declare the two intervals
$$I_{1}:=\Bigl[-\frac d2-\frac L2,\ -\frac d2+\frac L2\Bigr],\qquad I_{2}:=\Bigl[\frac d2-\frac L2,\ \frac d2+\frac L2\Bigr]$$
on the first spatial coordinate, measured in metres, whose **overlap region**
$O:=I_{1}\cap I_{2}=[\frac d2-\frac L2,\ -\frac d2+\frac L2]$ has length
$L-d>0$; let $g\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{2};\mathbb C)$ satisfy $\|g\|_{2}=1$ and
choose a Borel representative, which exists by completion of Borel Lebesgue measure
([[cor-lebesgue-sigma-algebra-is-the-completion-of-borel-lebesgue-measure]]).
Its amplitude unit is $\mathrm m^{-1}$ in the two-dimensional position measure;
declare the
**flat path amplitudes**
$$f_{1}:=L^{-1/2}\mathbf 1_{I_{1}},\qquad f_{2}:=L^{-1/2}\mathbf 1_{I_{2}}.$$
Define the declared path components by
$$\psi_{j}(x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}):=f_{j}(x_{1})\,g(x_{2},x_{3})\qquad(j=1,2).$$
In these SI conventions each $f_j$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-1/2}$ and each
$\psi_j$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-3/2}$, as required for a normalized position
wave function on $\mathbb R^3$; the probabilities below are dimensionless.
A **slab bin** is a set $B_{1}\times\mathbb R^{2}$ with $B_{1}\subseteq\mathbb R$
Borel. Then:

(a) $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\in H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with
$\|\psi_{1}\|=\|\psi_{2}\|=1$, so the declared data are admissible, and the
model is admissible at every phase: on $I_{1}\setminus I_{2}$ the combination $f_{1}+e^{i\varphi}f_{2}$ equals $L^{-1/2}$ independently of $\varphi$, and that region has length $d>0$. Since $\|g\|=1$, $\|\psi_1+e^{i\varphi}\psi_2\|^2=\|f_1+e^{i\varphi}f_2\|^2\ge d/L>0$.

(b) For every slab bin, with $N_{\varphi}:=\|f_{1}+e^{i\varphi}f_{2}\|^{2}=2+\frac{2(L-d)}{L}\cos\varphi$,
$$\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi)}(B_{1}\times\mathbb R^{2})=\frac{1}{N_{\varphi}}\int_{B_{1}}|f_{1}+e^{i\varphi}f_{2}|^{2}dx,\qquad \mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w)}(B_{1}\times\mathbb R^{2})=\frac{w\,|B_{1}\cap I_{1}|+(1-w)\,|B_{1}\cap I_{2}|}{L}.$$

(c) The coherent density $|f_{1}+e^{i\varphi}f_{2}|^{2}$ equals
$\frac{2(1+\cos\varphi)}{L}$ on $O$, equals $\frac1L$ on the symmetric
difference $I_{1}\triangle I_{2}$, and vanishes outside $I_{1}\cup I_{2}$;
consequently
$$\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi)}(O\times\mathbb R^{2})=\frac{(L-d)(1+\cos\varphi)}{L+(L-d)\cos\varphi},\qquad \mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi)}\bigl((I_{j}\setminus I_{3-j})\times\mathbb R^{2}\bigr)=\frac{d}{2L+2(L-d)\cos\varphi}$$
for $j=1,2$, and for the balanced which-path preparation $w=\frac12$
$$\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(1/2)}(O\times\mathbb R^{2})=\frac{L-d}{L},\qquad \mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(1/2)}\bigl((I_{j}\setminus I_{3-j})\times\mathbb R^{2}\bigr)=\frac{d}{2L}.$$

(d) At $\varphi=\pi$ the coherent law assigns probability zero to the whole
overlap region $O$ of positive length, while the balanced which-path law
assigns it probability $(L-d)/L>0$; every slab bin contained in $O$ has
coherent probability zero, every slab bin meeting $I_{1}\setminus I_{2}$ or
$I_{2}\setminus I_{1}$ in a set of positive length has positive coherent
probability, and every slab bin meeting $O$ in a set of positive length has
positive which-path probability.

The computation is exact in the declared model; it asserts no detector
response, no sampling model, no measured count and no laboratory realization.

items.title: A declared finite phase-averaging model reproduces the which-path law for orthogonal components
items.statement:
Adopt the declared two-path preparation and detection model
[[def-nrqm-interference-two-path-preparation-and-detection-model]] with path
components $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\ne0$ satisfying
$\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=0$ (orthogonal components), and the coherent
and which-path detection laws
[[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]]. Assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]), as required by the preparation and detection-law
suppliers. Fix an integer $n\ge2$
and declare the **finite phase-averaging model**: the relative phase takes the
$n$ values
$$\varphi_{k}:=\frac{2\pi k}{n}\qquad(k=0,1,\dots,n-1)$$
with equal statistical weight $1/n$, so that the averaged bin law of a Borel
set $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$ is
$$\bar p(B):=\frac1n\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{coh}}(\varphi_{k})}(B).$$
Put $N:=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}+\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}$ and $w_{*}:=\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}/N$.
Then:

(a) $\|\psi_{1}+e^{i\varphi_{k}}\psi_{2}\|^{2}=N$ for every $k$, so every
coherent preparation of the declared model has the same normalization $N$;

(b) the averaged cross term vanishes bin by bin:
$$\frac1n\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}2\operatorname{Re}\Bigl(e^{-i\varphi_{k}}\int_{B}\langle\psi_{1}(x),\psi_{2}(x)\rangle_{\mathbb C^{r}}dx\Bigr)=0 ;$$

(c) consequently $\bar p(B)=\mu^{G}_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}(w_{*})}(B)$ for every
Borel set $B$: the declared finite phase-averaging model reproduces the
which-path law with the norm weights, while each single phase shows the cross
term of [[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]].

The averaging over the phase is a declared statistical model of the preparation
ensemble in the sense of clause (ii) of the preparation and apparatus postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]; the computation asserts no
decoherence mechanism, no detector response, no counts and no empirical result,
and it does not cover the continuous uniform phase distribution, which would
require its own integral model.

items.title: Reported controlled double-slit electron diffraction with single-electron detection (Bach, Pope, Liou and Batelaan)
items.statement:
The paper reports, and the retained figures show, slit-selective probability
distributions: a single-slit central diffraction order in the P1 and P2
configurations and a double-slit distribution in the P12 configuration, with
weak double-slit contributions visible in the first diffraction order of the
nominal single-slit configurations, which the paper attributes to the finite
separation between the mask and the double-slit. For the mask-centred build-up
the figure captions report accumulated localized-event counts of 2, 7, 209,
1004 and 6235 in five successive images of the central five orders, the paper
describing the earliest images as appearing random and a pattern becoming
discernible at the largest counts, with a clearly visible pattern in the final
image. Each reported detection is a localized blob whose size represents the
localization error of the detection scheme; the accumulated distribution, not
any single event, carries the reported pattern.

references.title: R. Bach, D. Pope, S.-H. Liou and H. Batelaan, Controlled double-slit electron diffraction, arXiv:1210.6243v1, 22 October 2012 (8 pages); also published in New Journal of Physics 15 (2013) 033018. This item reports the exact preprint version retrieved and read: Sections 1-4 and figures 1-3, printed pages 1-8

items.physical_scope: A faithful report of the primary preprint R. Bach, D. Pope, S.-H. Liou and H. Batelaan, 'Controlled double-slit electron diffraction', arXiv:1210.6243v1 (22 October 2012): the reported apparatus, procedure, slit-selective distributions and single-electron event build-up, with the report's disclosed and undisclosed limitations. The item reports the source's observations and its qualified interpretation; it does not reanalyze the data, does not establish trial independence or single-electron occupancy, records no uncertainty budget beyond what the source supplies, and draws no conclusion about any physical theory.

empirical_result.observation: The report describes a 600 eV electron beam transmitted through a nanofabricated double-slit (two 50 nm slits, 280 nm center-to-center separation) and detected on a microchannel-plate/phosphor screen imaged by a CCD camera. Sweeping a movable mask downstream of the slit produces the slit-selective distributions the paper labels P1 (one slit), P12 (both slits) and P2 (the other slit); the paper reports weak double-slit contributions in the first diffraction order of the nominal single-slit configurations, attributed to the finite mask-to-slit separation. With the mask centred and the source intensity reduced to a detection rate of about 1 Hz, localized events were accumulated for about 2 hours; the figure captions report 2, 7, 209, 1004 and 6235 accumulated localized events in five successive central-five-order images, in which a diffraction pattern becomes discernible at the largest counts.
empirical_result.uncertainty: The report supplies no numerical uncertainty budget: no calibrated detector efficiency or background map, no numerical localization standard deviation (the blob size is said to represent the localization error, without a value), no arrival-process law or test of mutual independence of detections, no event-selection error rate, no statistical significance, confidence interval or fitted competing-model comparison, and no uncertainty on beam energy, slit dimensions or mask position. A source inconsistency in the mask height (5 micrometre by 10 micrometre in the body versus 5 micrometre by 20 micrometre in the figure 1 caption) is unresolved. The statements that at most one electron is present and that electron-electron interactions are eliminated rest on an average-separation estimate (2.3e6 m) rather than on a bound on two-electron occupancy. Approximate rate and duration values are not converted into an exact trial count, efficiency or calibrated rate.
empirical_result.conditions: Reported apparatus and settings: thermionic tungsten filament with electrostatic lenses producing a 600 eV beam; a 2 micrometre by 10 micrometre collimation aperture 16.5 cm from the source; the double-slit 30.5 cm beyond the collimation aperture, milled by a 30 keV Ga+ focused-ion-beam system into a 100 nm silicon-nitride membrane coated with about 2 nm of gold, with slits 50 nm wide, 280 nm centre-to-centre, 4 micrometre tall with a 150 nm support midway; a movable mask 5 micrometre wide (height given inconsistently as 10 or 20 micrometre) placed 230 micrometre downstream and driven by a piezoelectric actuator; electrostatic quadrupole magnification; a two-dimensional microchannel plate and phosphor screen imaged by a CCD camera, with each localized event recorded by a blob-detection scheme; mask-centred event accumulation at about 1 Hz over about 2 hours. These are reported specifications and settings, not independently recalibrated measurements.

items.title: What the worked items and the reported experiment of the examples page establish
items.statement:
**The two computations.** [[ex-nrqm-interference-ideal-flat-two-path-screen-distribution]]
computes, in the declared two-path model with flat product-form amplitudes, the
exact coherent and which-path probabilities of the overlap and outer regions of
the declared detection coordinate: at relative phase $\pi$ the coherent law
assigns probability zero to the whole overlap region while the balanced
which-path law assigns it positive probability, and a slab bin
$B_1\times\mathbb R^2$ has positive coherent probability at that phase
exactly when $|B_1\cap(I_1\triangle I_2)|>0$, where $I_1,I_2$ are the
declared intervals and $I_1\triangle I_2$ is their symmetric difference
(the two outer regions). Mere nonempty intersection does not suffice.
[[ex-nrqm-interference-uniform-phase-averaging]]
shows that for orthogonal path components a declared ensemble whose relative
phase is uniformly distributed over the finitely many $n$-th roots of unity has
the which-path law with the norm weights as its averaged law. Both are
conditional computations in the declared model under all the stated supplier
hypotheses, including Countable Choice and Choice, and the pair's detection laws
([[pthm-nrqm-interference-coherent-and-mixture-detection-laws]]); neither is a
dynamics, an environmental decoherence model, a detector response or a
statement about an apparatus.

**The reported experiment.** [[exp-nrqm-interference-bach-electron-double-slit]]
reports the primary preprint of Bach, Pope, Liou and Batelaan: a 600 eV
electron beam through a nanofabricated double-slit with slit-selective
distributions and a single-electron event build-up over 2, 7, 209, 1004 and
6235 accumulated localized events. The report supplies no calibrated
efficiency or background, no numerical localization error, no uncertainty for
its apparatus parameters, no occupancy bound and no statistical comparison
with a specified competing model; the mask-height inconsistency between its
body and its figure caption is recorded as unresolved. The item therefore
supports a qualitative operational account only, and its agreement with any
model is evidence about the combined model and apparatus assumptions, not a
proof of the framework, not a demonstration that every event is independent,
and not a demonstration that only one electron is in the apparatus at a time.

**What the page does not address.** No photon experiment is reported here; a
single-photon polarization or counting experiment belongs to the photon and
radiation page, and the classical wave comparison for light is a separate
declared model. No experiment testing the which-path or marker variants of the
arrangement is reported. No claim is made that the finite sample of the
reported experiment would distinguish the coherent from the which-path
recorded law; [[texp-nrqm-interference-finite-sample-fringe-failure]] shows
that both can fail or pass a finite-sample criterion and that coincident
recorded laws are indistinguishable by any criterion.

**Evidence status.** The page combines exact conditional computations with one
faithfully reported experiment. It contains no simulation presented as data,
no invented count, precision or significance, and no conclusion about nature;
the empirical qualifications of the report are carried in its Observations and
Uncertainty sections and are not strengthened here.
